title: Complete Binary-to-Unary Conversion
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $a,N,v\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $x$ be a finite word over the schedule alphabet. Choose a base configuration on input $x$, an input-head position $p$, an integer guide-head position $g$, and guide-tape contents $\gamma\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{OblSymbol})$. For every bit word $w$ of little-endian value $v$, running the length-only schedule machine from the setup configuration in the budget-start phase, with budget head at $|w|+1$ on the captured clock tape of $w$ and unary head at $N+1$ on the unary tape with $N$ markers, for exactly $(v+1)(2|w|+(a+1)+4)$ steps yields the setup configuration in the unary-start phase with the same base configuration, input-head position, and guide tape and head, with budget head still at $|w|+1$ and unary head at $N+(a+1)(v+1)+1$. Its budget tape is the captured clock tape of some bit word $w'$ with $|w'|=|w|$, and its unary tape has $N+(a+1)(v+1)$ markers.
hypotheses_covered: Input word x over the schedule alphabet
replaced:
Let $w$ be a bit word of little-endian value $v$ and let $N \in \bbn$.  From a setup
configuration in the budget-start phase with budget head at $|w|+1$ over the captured
clock tape of $w$ and unary head at $N+1$ over the unary tape with $N$ markers, exactly
$(v+1)\,\bigl(2|w| + (a+1) + 4\bigr)$ steps reach the unary-start phase with unary head
at $N + (a+1)(v+1) + 1$ over the unary tape with $N + (a+1)(v+1)$ markers, the budget
tape being the captured clock tape of some bit word $w'$ with $|w'| = |w|$ (the word
keeps its full width as its high bits become zero); the guide tape and head and the
input head are unchanged.
